text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)

THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW Business Council of Australia president Stan Wallis has criticised the Federal Government for its lack of a strategic plan on economic reform. Speaking at the launch of a restructuring of the BCA, Wallis urged for tax reform and a consistent industry polcy. Page 1.

-- Reporting a 14 per cent rise in interim net profits to A$1.14 billion for the first half, National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus warned the days of record profits in the industry may be coming to a close. Bank's share prices faltered yesterdy on the back of the warning, with the Banks and Finance Index down 1.1 per cent. Page 1.

-- Santos Ltd managing director Ross Adler said yesterday the company's credentials as a resources growth stock could lift as a result of a 25 per cent lift in oil and gas production to 50 million barrels, and "company-making" oil plays in the Timor Sea. Pag 37.

-- Kevin Parry, the former head of the Parry Corp which collapsed after the 1987 stockmarket crash, announced this week he had finalised a A$128 million deal to redevelop Armenia's Zod mine in conjunction with the Armenian Government and North American minerFirst Dynasty Mines. Page 37.

-- Colonial Ltd's float is set to hit the history books as one of the most oversubscribed floats in Australia's corporate history, with one fund manager claiming he'd not heard of anything as oversubscribed as Colonial. While bids of A$3.00 and A$3.10 are epected for shares, some institutions are rumoured to be looking at bidding as high as A$3.50 a share. Page 38.

-- Mayne Nickless Express chief executive officer Phil Smith has suddenly departed, being replaced by former head of Mayne Nickless subsidiary Armaguard Graeme Turner. The move is part of a high-level management shake-up resulting from the company's effortsto merge all of its express freight and courier businesses into one operation. Page 39

THE AUSTRALIAN Confusion over the Federal Budget's tax changes in the A$60 billion share-based derivatives industry continued to take its toll on the share market yesterday, as key players in the industry consulted the Australian Tax Office for clarification. As the inustry described the changes as an "ambush", the ATO refused to back down on the proposal. Page 25.

-- National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus said yesterday difficult industry conditions, including a flat economy, shrinking interest margins, and fierce competition, threatened to signal an end to the Bank's remarkable earnings performance of th 1990s, which was proved again yesterday with a 14 per cent surge in interim net profit to A$1.14 billion. Page 25.

-- Industry leaders in Australia's A$4 billion home appliance market - Email Ltd, Southcorp Holdings Ltd, and New Zealand's Fisher & Paykel Ltd - are expected to feel the impact of the launch into the market by Korean manufacturing heavyweight Daewoo Electronics Co. Page 25.

-- Shares in the Seven Network have continued to climb on the back of optimism over the company's investment in Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and speculation of imminent changes to media ownership laws. Seven's shares have increased 36 per cent since July, when the MM deal was announced. Page 26

-- Employees of tour operator CTC Package Holidays Pty Ltd, which trades as CTC Cruise Lines, were formally dismissed on Wednesday and will have a claim launched on their behalf by the Australian Services Union, as the company has been put into provisional lquidation following a cash crisis that saw all upcoming trips cancelled. Page 27.

-- Novus Petroleum chairman John FitzGerald told the company's annual meeting in Sydney yesterday that early results at two exploration wells - Singa-1 in Indonesia and Miriwah-1 in Pakistan - were cause for optimism. Shares in the oil and gas producer havelifted in recent weeks thanks to interest in the Singa field and recent acquisitions. Page 27.

-- THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD The members of the Business Council of Australia executive committee, including president Stan Wallis, said yesterday Australia's political leaders, with the exception of Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett, had no long-term vision for the country. The member believe the Howard Government has no strategic policy for industry. Page 27.

-- While the National Australia Bank yesterday became the first sharemarket company to make a billion dollar interim profit - the Bank posted net profit for the six months to March of A$1.14 billion - the celebrations were muted due to its surprisingly poor erformance in its home market. Page 27.

-- Following investigations by the Australian Stock Exchange, the Australian Securities Commission, and the fraud squad into alleged unauthorised trading in the accounts of ReitreInvest clients, the ASC has warned investors to be actively involved in their ivestments to prevent unauthorised trading in their accounts. Page 29.

-- After stockbrokers held meetings yesterday with their staff to discuss the impact of the Federal Government's new rules on franking credits, the Australian Stock Exchange has requested an urgent meeting with Federal Treasurer Peter Costello to clarify itsposition on the issue. Page 29.

-- Bankers Trust International, the major unit-holder in the Rural Property Trust, last night launched legal proceedings against the manager of Rural Property Trust, Rural and Agricultural Management, alleging deceptive and misleading conduct. Page 29.

-- Analysts are predicting that stock prices in Woodside Petroleum, which have already climbed from A$7 last year to a new high of A$11.15 yesterday, may go as high as A$14. Macquarie Equities analyst Peter Best said yesterday there are plenty of reasons to invest in Woodside, which has benefited from a number of happy coincidences. Page 30.

THE AGE The Business Council of Australia said yesterday it would be prepared to begin developing a national vision outlining a framework to assist Australia to become "a more prosperous and equitable society" after it criticised the Howard Government for lackingany strategies for industry. Page B1.

-- It has been revealed Newcrest's former managing director John Quinn, who abruptly left the company on Wednesday, had faith in the company's future, as his 12 May directors interest showed he purchased an additional 165,000 options on 5 May on top of his eisting 280,000 options listed in the annual report. Page B1.

-- National Australia Bank has enjoyed a A$1.14 billion interim net profit on the back of good performances in its overseas banking network. Managing director Don Argus said the group's network of four regional banks in Britain and Ireland increased profit by 34 per cent, while the New Zealand business returned an extra 155 per cent. Page B1.

-- National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus has turned the Bank around into one of the 10 most profitable banks in the world, yet Argus revealed yesterday he still expects more. Argus said NAB had received feedback that it was "top of the list" fr several international merchant banks hoping to join the Australian arena following the Federal Government's policy shift. Page B1.

-- Ziff-Davis Inc, the world most successful computer magazine publisher and owner of the world rights to PC Magazine and PC Week, yesterday withdrew its publishing licenses from Kerry Packer's Australian Consolidated Press. Ziff-Davies said Australian readrs would have to be content with US editions of the magazines until local versions were published. Page B1.

-- The Adsteam Marine ST.AX float was officially opened yesterday, and was swamped by investors, with institutional investors expecting to get over half the shares in the A$160 million float they ask for. Shareholders in parent company Residual Assco will get ther full 20 per cent. Page B1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
